newsitem.title: USA: Fla. amendment group says court ignored voter will.
newsitem.headline: Fla. amendment group says court ignored voter will.

text.p: The sponsors of a tax-limiting amendment said the Florida Supreme Court ignored voters' wishes when it struck down the proposal Thursday.
"What upsets me most is that the court chose not to trust the will of the people," said Kate Zichella, an organizer in southwest Florida for the Tax Cap Committee.
The group collected the voter signatures needed for a referendum on three constitutional amendments.

One would have required voter approval for new taxes. The second would require local and state governments to compensate property owners if a government action decreased the property's value. The third was a technical amendment needed to make the compensation proposal legal.

The state Supreme Court struck down all three Thursday, ruling that they failed to meet requirements that ballot language be clear and not misleading, and that the amendments address a narrowly defined issue.
Tax Cap Chairman David Biddulph said he was especially shocked at the ruling because he thought the group had addressed the problems the court raised when it rejected a similar proposal in 1994.

"This is purely political," Biddulph said. "The court has gone beyond their constitutional mandate. They have violated the simple constitutional requirement that the power to reform the constitution is reserved to the people."
He said the group had not decided whether to seek reworded amendments.
Opponents, a coalition of municipal governments, environmentalists and city planners, said the amendments would create financial gridlock.
Florida Audubon Society President Clay Henderson said the ruling was correct and necessary.
"The effect of those amendments would have been to neutralize a generation of environmental protection and growth management laws. We are delighted," Henderson said.
